examples.en: We decided to hold a family meeting this weekend.

examples.ko: 우리는 가족회의에서 여름 여행 장소를 정했어요.
examples.en: We chose our summer trip destination at a family meeting.
The family meeting starts after dinner.
A family meeting was suddenly called, so I felt a bit nervous.

examples.ko: 가족회의 때 모두 자기 의견을 말해요.
examples.en: At family meetings, everyone says their own opinion.
In our house, we decide big matters through a family meeting.

explain: '가족회의를 열다/하다'처럼 말해요. 회사의 딱딱한 회의와 달리 집에서 편하게 의견을 나누는 자리라는 느낌이에요. 이사, 여행, 용돈처럼 가족이 함께 정할 일에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: We hold a family meeting in the evening.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual alternative to '열다'.

phrases.en: Sunday evening is our family meeting time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 때가 있을 때 '시간'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '시간' when there is a set time for it.

phrases.en: We decide the trip date at a family meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 정하는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how something gets decided.

explain_en: You say it as '가족회의를 열다/하다'. Unlike a stiff business meeting, it feels like a relaxed time at home to share opinions. It suits things a family decides together, such as moving, trips or allowances.

examples.en: My father goes to the golf course every Sunday.
The scenery at this golf course is really nice.
It takes an hour by car to get to the golf course.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 회사 사람들과 골프장을 예약했어요.
examples.en: I booked the golf course with my coworkers for this weekend.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 골프장이 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the golf course closed.

explain: 골프는 '치다'와 함께 써서 '골프를 치다'라고 해요. 골프장에서 한 바퀴 도는 것을 '라운딩'이라고도 하고, 골프장 이름 뒤에는 'CC'를 자주 붙여요. '골프 치러 가다'처럼 목적을 말할 때는 '골프장' 없이도 돼요.

phrases.en: I play golf with a friend on weekends.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'chida' for playing golf.

phrases.en: I go to the golf course tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 골프를 하러 그곳으로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for going there to play golf.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the golf course

phrases.en: My father went to play golf.
phrases.nuance_en: When stating the purpose, you can say it without 'golf course'.

explain_en: Golf pairs with '치다' (hit), so you say '골프를 치다'. Playing a round at the course is also called '라운딩', and course names often end in 'CC'. For purpose you can say '골프 치러 가다' (go to play golf) without mentioning the course.

examples.ko: 그전 같으면 이런 일에 화를 냈을 거예요.
examples.en: In the past, I would have gotten angry about something like this.

examples.ko: 그전과 비교하면 요즘은 훨씬 여유가 있어요.
examples.en: Compared to before, I have much more breathing room these days.
I sometimes think of the neighborhood where I lived before.
I have changed a lot from who I was before.

examples.ko: 그전엔 매일 걸어서 출근했는데 지금은 차로 가요.
examples.en: I used to walk to work every day, but now I go by car.

explain: '예전'이 막연히 오래전을 가리킨다면 '그전'은 앞에서 말한 일이나 때보다 앞선 시간을 가리켜요. '그전에는, 그전 같으면'처럼 지금과 비교할 때 자주 나와요. '그 전'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 회의는 열 시예요. 그 전에 오세요.
phrases.en: The meeting is at ten. Please come before that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 말한 때보다 먼저라는 뜻으로 띄어 써서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form, meaning earlier than the time just mentioned.

phrases.en: Korean has become much easier than before.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare the past with now.

phrases.en: Before that, I couldn't eat spicy food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전 상황을 말하며 지금과 다르다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a past situation that differs from now.

explain_en: While '예전' vaguely points to long ago, '그전' points to a time before the event or time just mentioned. It often appears when comparing with now, as in '그전에는' and '그전 같으면'. You will also see it written as '그 전'.

examples.en: At night the temperature drops.
Interest rates have gone down lately, so loans got easier.

examples.ko: 시험이 너무 어려우면 평균 점수가 낮아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the test is too hard, the average score can go down.
When you press the button, the desk slowly lowers.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되자 바닷물 온도가 많이 낮아졌어요.
examples.en: When winter came, the sea water temperature dropped a lot.

explain: '높아지다'의 반대말이고, 높이·온도·점수·수준처럼 위아래로 재는 것에 두루 써요. 소리는 '작아지다'와 달리 '낮아지다'라고 하면 음의 높낮이가 내려간다는 뜻이 돼요. 값이 내려갈 때는 '싸지다'나 '내려가다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The temperature is lower than yesterday.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the weather has gotten colder.

phrases.en: If you don't study, your score gets lower.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a test score goes down.

phrases.en: Prices are getting lower little by little these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 변하는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the change is still going on.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '높아지다' and works for anything measured up and down, such as height, temperature, scores and level. For voices, '낮아지다' means the pitch goes down, unlike '작아지다', which means quieter. For prices, people also say '싸지다' or '내려가다'.

examples.en: No hot water comes out of the tap.
Please mix hot and cold water half and half.
On cold days, a hot shower is the best.

explain: 반대말은 '찬물'이에요. 말할 때는 '뜨거운 물'이나 '따뜻한 물'을 더 자주 쓰고, 안내문이나 설명서에서는 '온수'를 많이 봐요. '더운물'은 샤워, 세수처럼 씻을 때 자연스럽게 나와요.

phrases.example: 아침에 따뜻한 물을 한 잔 마셔요.
phrases.en: I drink a glass of warm water in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더운물'을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 다른 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common alternative to say 더운물 in speech.

phrases.en: Be careful with the hot water.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels hotter than 더운물.

phrases.en: In winter, I wash my face with warm water.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural use when washing.

explain_en: The opposite is '찬물' (cold water). In speech people often say '뜨거운 물' or '따뜻한 물', and signs or manuals often use '온수'. '더운물' comes up naturally when washing, such as showering or washing your face.

examples.en: My daughter enters elementary school this year.
My daughter wakes me up every morning.
I went to the park with my daughter.
I bought a new bike for my daughter.
When I think of my daughter, I get energy.

explain: 자기 딸을 남에게 말할 때 '딸'보다 부드럽게 들려서 '딸아이'를 많이 써요. 아들은 '아들아이'도 쓰지만 보통 그냥 '아들'이라고 해요. 남의 딸을 높여 말할 때는 '따님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My daughter is a middle school student now.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, more basic word than 딸아이.

phrases.en: Your daughter is so pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 딸을 높여서 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely refer to someone else's daughter.

phrases.example: 우리 딸아이는 책 읽는 것을 좋아해요.
phrases.en: My daughter loves reading books.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 우리 makes it a warm way to say 'my daughter'.

explain_en: Parents often say 딸아이 when talking about their own daughter to others since it sounds softer than 딸. For a son, 아들아이 exists but people usually just say 아들. To honor someone else's daughter, use 따님.

examples.en: I'm going to get my hair done at the salon this weekend.
I went to the salon to get my hair done before the interview.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 머리하고 나서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: After getting our hair done together, my friend and I took photos.

explain: 커트인지 파마인지 염색인지 말하지 않고 두루 쓸 때 편한 입말이에요. 구체적으로 말하려면 '머리를 자르다', '파마하다', '염색하다'를 써요. 집에서 머리를 씻고 말리는 건 '머리를 감다', '머리를 말리다'라서 '머리하다'가 아니에요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow I am going to the salon to get my hair done.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-러 가다'를 붙여서 머리를 하려고 간다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -러 가다 says you go in order to get your hair done.
phrases.en_equiv: to go get one's hair done

phrases.en: You got your hair done. It suits you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 모양이 바뀐 것을 보고 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used casually when you notice someone's new hairstyle.

phrases.en: I got a new hairstyle and I feel good.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 새로 makes it clear you changed your style.

explain_en: A casual word for visiting a salon without saying whether it's a cut, perm, or dye. To be specific, say '머리를 자르다' (cut), '파마하다' (perm), or '염색하다' (dye). Washing or drying your hair at home is '머리를 감다' or '머리를 말리다', not '머리하다'.

examples.ko: 보리밥에 나물을 넣고 고추장으로 비벼 먹어요.
어릴 때 할머니가 보리밥을 자주 해 주셨어요.

explain: 쌀로만 지은 '쌀밥', 여러 곡식을 섞은 '잡곡밥'과 구별해서 말해요. 식당에서는 '보리밥 정식'이나 '보리밥집'처럼 나물과 함께 나오는 메뉴로 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I eat barley rice for my health.
phrases.nuance_en: Rice goes with the verb 먹다.

phrases.en: I ordered the barley rice set for lunch.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on restaurant menus.

phrases.en: There is a famous barley rice restaurant at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that serves barley rice.

explain_en: It is distinguished from '쌀밥' (rice only) and '잡곡밥' (mixed grains). At restaurants you often see it as a set meal served with namul, such as '보리밥 정식' or at a '보리밥집'.
